# Security

- SEC-009: Every read or change of a user's data is limited to that user's data in the query itself, in the application and data layers, not only in the endpoint; the user's id is the token's sub claim, which the fallback policy requires (unique within one issuer, so an app that trusts more than one keys on the issuer and sub together), and another user's item answers 404, as one that doesn't exist does.
- SEC-019: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object and performs any action on the object should implement object-level authorization checks. Use the authorization mechanism to check that the logged-in user has access to perform the requested action on the record in every function that uses an input from the client to access a record in the database. ASVS 8.2.2 and 8.3.1: data-specific access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific data items, and authorization rules are enforced at a trusted service layer. To store information per user, use the sub or oid claim alone (with tid for routing or sharding if needed), and don't identify a user by human-readable data.
